text:
Samir K: heads up — h100-e2e shard 12 turned red on the nightly. Failing intermittently with OOM during the XLA compile step (not token generation).
Maria L: ugh, saw that too. Is this the new runtime bump from yesterday?
Samir K: looks like it started after runtime@v2.14.2 landed (PR 4821). Fail rate ~3/10 runs.
Alex W: can you paste the stack/log snippet?
Samir K: here — main error is 'ResourceExhaustedError: Ran out of memory while trying to allocate XLA buffer' around xla_cpu_compilation.cc:
```
2026-03-17T04:12:11Z ERROR: XLA allocation failed: requested=1.8G available=1.2G
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/work/runner/xla_compiler.py", line 142, in compile_for_device
    compiled = backend.compile(... )
  File "/opt/xla/backend.cc", line 87, in Allocate
    raise ResourceExhaustedError('out of memory')
```
Samir K: also saw this message from driver side on node: "nvml: failed to allocate page-locked memory" once.
CI Bot: build 21244 (h100-e2e/shard=12) failed — test-suite/large-batch (xla compile) — retry available. /rerun to trigger.
Maria L: hypothesis: concurrent CI runners on the same host are starving pinned host memory used by XLA. We recently bumped parallelism to 4 per node for e2e.
Jin T: can we repro locally with parallel shards? Try setting XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.5 and TF_FORCE_GPU_ALLOW_GROWTH=1 to see if it stabilizes.
Alex W: also try reducing per-process batch size by 2 to confirm it's memory pressure. If that helps, we can gate the runtime bump behind lower default parallelism.
Samir K: quick triage plan: (1) rerun failing shard twice to confirm flakiness; (2) run a canary with env overrides on a single node; (3) if repro, bisect runtime commits between v2.14.0..v2.14.2. Who can run the canary?
Maria L: I can kick off the canary with env overrides. Command I used yesterday:
```bash
# spawn ephemeral canary job
cictl run --job h100-e2e --shard 12 --env XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.5 --env TF_FORCE_GPU_ALLOW_GROWTH=1 --parallelism 1
```
Maria L: starting it now, will report back in ~20m.
Samir K: thanks. If it passes, we probably need a mitigations PR to lower default parallelism and add env flag in the test harness. If it fails consistently, next step is bisect.
Alex W: FYI I noticed one machine had older driver 535.54 vs cluster standard 535.86 — not sure if related but worth checking.
Jin T: please add the node list to the issue. Maybe the provisioning job didn't roll drivers.
Maria L: canary finished: PASSED on single-node with memory fraction tweak. Rerun of two previous failures: 1/2 still failed.
Samir K: sounds like concurrency-related mem pressure. Maria, can you open a quick issue with logs + node IDs + link to failing build? I'll prepare a short PR to set parallelism=2 for e2e until we patch the runtime.
Maria L: created issue #726 — link: https://redwood-infra/issue/726 — added logs and node list.
CI Bot: triggered rerun of build 21244 (requested by Samir K).
Alex W: pinging infra to check driver rollouts — @ops-team can you confirm uniform driver versions on h100 pool?
Samir K: thanks everyone. If anyone has spare cycles, thumbs up to PR draft: reduce-e2e-parallelism-#4830. I'll link it here when ready. :thumbsup:
Maria L: ack, will watch the PR and help validate once merged.
Alex W: good catch, team. Short-term mitigation looks reasonable.
